ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.89 excess distance fare to the rider's original payment method; issue the driver a notification-duty reminder and log the uninformed/refused reroute on his route compliance record.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: no threats, harassment, sexual remarks or dangerous-driving allegations in the chat [F7–F11] or complaint; nothing in F15 indicates an accident. safety_concern = none.

Route deviation: actual 14.9 km vs optimal 10.7 km = +4.2 km [F1], far above the 1 km tolerance (RD-1). The single off-route segment 21:43–21:50 drove JALAN BUKIT MERAH → KAMPONG BAHRU ROAD → TELOK BLANGAH ROAD → HENDERSON ROAD, adding 3.70 km [F3] — this is the segment that produced the excess.

Traffic reason (RD-4): the record shows no incident near the route [F14] and Ayer Rajah Expressway was flowing at speed band 7 (60–69 km/h) during the trip window [F12]. The driver's claimed congestion [F7/F11] is contradicted by the traffic data, so the reroute had no traffic justification under RD-4/RD-2.

Consent (RD-5 / RD-3): the driver asked to go via Telok Blangah Road [F7] and the rider expressly refused — "No, I'm not okay with that. Please stay on Ayer Rajah Expressway" [F8] — before the segment began at 21:43. The rider's own message is the consent test, and a refusal is not consent; the driver's post-trip assertion of agreement [F11] is a claim, not consent. The segment therefore counts in full and none of the 3.70 km is exempt.

Amount (RD-2 / §1.3, C3): refundable km = deviation − exempt km = 4.18 km − 0 = 4.18 km; refund = 4.18 km × $1.4098/km = $5.89, matching the billed excess distance fare [F4]. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded; surge was 1.0× so SURGE clauses do not apply [F5]. No traffic reason also records a driver violation (RD-2). The driver's profile shows 2 upheld disputes but 0 upheld route deviations, so the RD-6 90-day repeat-deviation add-on does not apply — no flag_account. This is a first notification-related incident, so a reminder and compliance log entry under RD-7, no formal warning. Amount is under $10, so the system ruling is final (TH-1, C1/DISP-001).

Evidence status: sufficient — GPS coverage [F1–F3], fare build-up [F4–F6], fully timestamped chat [F10] and traffic data [F12–F14] settle every element.

segment_findings.reason: Driver proposed going via Telok Blangah Road [F7]; rider expressly refused before the segment began ('Please stay on Ayer Rajah Expressway', F8). No rider consent under RD-5/RD-3, and no traffic reason under RD-4 (F12 shows AXE flowing at band 7, no incidents F14). The whole 3.70 km addition counts; not exempt.

element_findings.reason: Ayer Rajah Expressway speed band 7 (60–69 km/h) during 21:29–22:01 and no incidents recorded; the driver's claimed congestion is contradicted by the traffic data.
Rider refused the proposed Telok Blangah route in a timestamped message before the segment started; the driver's post-trip statement of agreement is a claim, not consent.
Driver profile shows 0 upheld route deviations in the last 90 days, so no account flag.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip written statement that the rider agreed and that the route was faster — a claim, not consent, and contradicted by the traffic data [F12] and the rider's refusal [F8].
Driver's claimed building-up traffic on Ayer Rajah Expressway is contradicted by speed band 7 and no recorded incidents [F12, F14]; no RD-4 traffic reason.
